title: Large numbers, rounding and estimating
summary: Read and build numbers in the millions in groups of three digits, round to the nearest 10, 100 or 1000 by looking at the next place, and estimate a sum before you work it out.
guide: We split big numbers into groups of three digits from the right: ones, thousands and {{term:million}}s. The name of each group is written above the chart, and in a written number a comma separates the groups: 2,050,300.
To read a number, read each group like a 3-digit number and then say the group's name: "two million, fifty thousand, three hundred". If a place is empty, the number shows a 0.
Places bigger than the thousands show counters instead of blocks. Each counter is worth its column's value.

To {{term:round}} to the nearest hundred, find the nearest whole hundred. The place you round to is outlined, and the place to its right is dashed: look only at the dashed digit. 0 to 4: the outlined digit stays the same. 5 to 9: it goes up by one. Every place to the right becomes 0.
In Year 5 and 6 you round all the way to the nearest 1,000,000 in exactly the same way.
To {{term:estimate}} means to find an answer that is close, using rounded numbers, before working it out exactly. It tells you if your exact answer makes sense.

build-million.title: Two million, fifty thousand, three hundred
build-million.prompt: A house costs two million, fifty thousand, three hundred pounds. Build this number. Think first: which places will hold a 0?
build-million.hint: Go group by group. Millions: 2. Thousands: 050 (fifty). Ones: 300 (three hundred).
build-million.success: Well done! 2,050,300: two million, fifty thousand, three hundred.
build-million.why: Why do we write "fifty thousand" as 050 in the thousands group, not just 50?
build-million.model: Every group has three places: hundreds, tens and ones. In fifty thousand, the hundred thousands are empty, the ten thousands hold 5 and the thousands hold 0. Without the first 0, the 5 would land in the wrong place and the number would be 250,300, which is much smaller.

feedback.dropped-zero: This is 250,300: two hundred and fifty thousand. "Two million" means a 2 in the millions place.
feedback.zero-moved: Your 5 is in the hundred thousands: that's five hundred thousand. Fifty thousand is a 5 in the ten thousands.
feedback.fifty-as-five: That's five thousand. Fifty thousand is a 5 in the ten thousands.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Check the groups one at a time.
feedback.too-small: Not enough yet. Look at the millions and the thousands.
feedback.empty: Use the + buttons to build the number.

round-hundred.title: Round to the nearest hundred
round-hundred.prompt: A school has 4682 books. Round this to the nearest hundred: change the number on the chart until it shows your answer. Predict first: 4600 or 4700?
round-hundred.hint: Look at the dashed place (the tens): it's 8. 8 is 5 or more, so the hundreds go up by one, and the tens and ones become 0.
round-hundred.success: That's right! 4682 is closer to 4700 than to 4600.
round-hundred.why: Why do we only look at the tens digit when rounding to the nearest hundred?
round-hundred.model: 4682 is between 4600 and 4700. Halfway is 4650. The tens digit tells us whether we're past halfway: 8 tens means 4680, which is past 4650, so it's closer to 4700. The ones are too small to change the answer.

feedback.rounded-down: You wrote 4600. But the tens digit is 8, so we're past halfway (4650). The hundreds go up by one.
feedback.to-ten: That's rounding to the nearest ten. We want the nearest hundred: both the tens and the ones become 0.
feedback.to-thousand: That's rounding to the nearest thousand. We want the nearest hundred.
feedback.kept-rest: You put the hundreds up correctly. Now make the tens and ones 0.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Only the hundreds go up by one.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Look at the dashed digit.
feedback.empty: You cleared the number. Start again.

round-thousand.title: Round to the nearest thousand
round-thousand.prompt: A town has 352,481 people. Round this to the nearest thousand. Careful which place you look at!
round-thousand.hint: The dashed place is the hundreds: 4. 4 is less than 5, so the thousands stay 2. The hundreds, tens and ones become 0.
round-thousand.why: Hassan said, "8 is big, so we round up", and wrote 353,000. What would you tell him?
round-thousand.model: When rounding to the nearest thousand, only the hundreds digit matters, because it shows whether we're past 352,500, halfway between 352,000 and 353,000. The hundreds digit is 4: 352,400 and a bit, not halfway yet. The 8 is in the tens, so it's only worth 80.

feedback.rounded-up: Did you look at the 8, like Hassan? Only the dashed place (the hundreds) matters: it's 4, so round down.
feedback.to-ten-thousand: That's rounding to the nearest ten thousand. The thousands digit should stay.
feedback.to-ten: That's rounding to the nearest ten. The hundreds, tens and ones should all become 0.
feedback.to-hundred: That's rounding to the nearest hundred. We want the nearest thousand.
feedback.empty: You cleared the number. Start again.

estimate-sum.title: Estimate first
estimate-sum.prompt: Reza has 3890 points and Zahra has 2140. Before adding exactly, {{term:estimate}}: round each number to the nearest thousand and add. Write your estimate.
estimate-sum.hint: 3890 is close to 4000 (the hundreds digit is 8). 2140 is close to 2000 (the hundreds digit is 1). Now 4000 + 2000.
estimate-sum.success: That's right! About 6000. The exact total is 6030. How close!
estimate-sum.why: Fatemeh added exactly and got 5030. How does your estimate help her?
estimate-sum.model: Our estimate is about 6000. 5030 is a whole thousand less, so Fatemeh probably forgot to carry from the hundreds into the thousands. An estimate is quick, and it tells us whether an exact answer makes sense.

feedback.exact: That's the exact total. Well worked out! But here we want the estimate: 4000 + 2000.
feedback.both-down: Did you round 3890 to 3000? Its hundreds digit is 8, so it's closer to 4000.
feedback.rounded-one: You rounded only one of the numbers. Round both to the nearest thousand.
feedback.too-big: Too big. Round each number to the nearest thousand.
feedback.too-small: Too small. Round each number to the nearest thousand.
feedback.empty: Write your estimate in the box.
